product.name: The Ascent of Karl
product.promise: Shape Karl's journey through what you combine, collect the history and fates you uncover, and hear the narrator turn every success and disaster into his story.
product.primaryPurpose: An interactive story where combining is how the player chooses what Karl tries, discovers, invents, solves, and becomes.
product.northStar: Authored-content completion percentage across archived lives.
completionDefinition: Generated inventions do not enter the denominator; authored consequences they unlock count.
hardBoundaries: Implementation may proceed across approved targets, but no target behavior is `production` until its advancement gate passes.
The product is entertainment, not curriculum or assessment.
Historical claims require curated canonical content and verified sources.
Generated graphs and implementation evidence never override human product authority.
Accessibility is a release gate across every capability.
Current truth and approved target must remain explicitly separate.
openDecisions: Production model provider and hosting architecture.
Numerical thresholds before measured playtest baselines.
Long-term breadth of open-ended sandbox play.

crossCutting.collectionRecordsStory: Collection is the visible record of the story the player authored.
crossCutting.narratorThreeDimensions: Humour, guidance, and the account of who Karl becomes are equally required narrator outcomes.
crossCutting.history: Historical logic makes the story world credible; generated inventions carry no historical claim.
crossCutting.karl: Karl is the recognisable comic mascot, visibly marked by accumulated choices.
crossCutting.accessibility: Equivalent information and action channels plus WCAG AA gate every capability.
crossCutting.sandbox: Open-ended experimentation is a secondary objective integrated into authored progression.
crossCutting.generatedGameplay: Models propose typed run-local gameplay; deterministic validation owns truth and effects.
crossCutting.onlineTarget: Active play may become online-required only after the production-readiness gate.
crossCutting.svelteParity: The post-playtest Svelte replacement preserves behavior, semantics, visuals, accessibility, events, and saves before redesign.

currentArchitecture: TypeScript and Vite with a deterministic content-driven core.
Complete authored gameplay can run without a backend.
Public root forces improvisation off; the unlisted playtest enables the deterministic offline invention floor.
Worker URLs are absent from shipped bundles.
targetArchitecture: Product truth infrastructure precedes and governs player-facing changes.
Replace the UI with Svelte in one coordinated migration now.
Generated gameplay remains typed, deterministic-validated, run-local, and historically non-authoritative.
Active play becomes online-required only after backend production readiness.
Typed product events remain local until telemetry hosting and consent are approved.
authorityAnchors: Shape Karl's journey through what you combine, collect the history and fates you uncover, and hear the narrator turn every success and disaster into his story.
The Ascent of Karl is an **interactive story**.
The product north star is the player's **authored-content completion percentage**
The narrator's humour, guidance, and account of who Karl becomes are equally important.
The approved target is online-required active play.
Martin explicitly lifted the pre-playtest implementation freeze on 2026-08-16.
Implementation may proceed across approved targets, but no target behavior is `production` until its advancement gate passes.

capabilities.name: Begin a life
capabilities.purpose: Start one distinct archived Karl life and reach meaningful play quickly.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player understands the available starting possibilities and begins a viable but meaningfully varied life.
capabilities.currentTruth: New, continue, and restart flows exist; starting elements and sidequests are not governed by a formal seeded viability contract.
capabilities.approvedTarget: A stored deterministic seed selects a bounded starting subset and sidequests while guaranteeing viable authored progression.
qualitativeAcceptance: Players notice that a new life differs.
Players understand the starting possibilities without explanation.
Every generated seed retains a viable authored path.

lifecycle.advancementGate: Define and exhaustively verify seeded starting-pool and sidequest viability before implementation.

capabilities.name: Choose and combine
capabilities.purpose: Give the player the primary language for deciding what Karl tries.
capabilities.playerOutcome: A selected pair produces a meaningful result, reaction, consequence, or clue.
capabilities.currentTruth: The player selects two elements. Canonical recipes win; otherwise the engine returns a specific verdict and optional bounded improvisation.
capabilities.approvedTarget: Every valid attempt produces meaningful yield: a new outcome or a specific humour, guidance, or story response.
qualitativeAcceptance: Most valid attempts produce meaningful yield.
Generic silence never follows an attempt.
The player can distinguish result, reaction, and next possibility.

lifecycle.advancementGate: External playtest must establish where attempts still feel empty or arbitrary.

capabilities.name: Canonical discovery
capabilities.purpose: Deliver a collectible authored story milestone that expands future possibilities.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player recognises a new canonical result, sees collection progress, and understands that the world has expanded.
capabilities.currentTruth: Canonical discoveries can carry flavor, historical notes, flags, need resolution, rarity, and age-up effects.
capabilities.approvedTarget: The discovery's newness, future utility, Chronicle entry, and persistent completion effect are immediately legible.
qualitativeAcceptance: Players recognise the result as new.
Players understand that it expands future possibilities.
Visible collection progress feels valuable.

lifecycle.advancementGate: The dual collection model must define canonical completion and save compatibility.

capabilities.name: Invention
capabilities.purpose: Provide alternative progression when a player's unscripted idea is plausible or productively absurd.
capabilities.playerOutcome: A player-owned invention remains distinct from canon and can meaningfully affect this life.
capabilities.currentTruth: A deterministic offline invention floor exists behind a production-off flag. Optional network copy may improve name and flavor only.
capabilities.approvedTarget: A model may propose typed run-local gameplay under deterministic validation; accepted inventions may solve needs and unlock authored consequences without historical claims.
qualitativeAcceptance: Inventions offer credible alternative progress.
Players understand inventions are not historical canon.
The result feels caused by the player's unscripted choice.

lifecycle.advancementGate: External improvisation playtest, deterministic gameplay validator, and production backend readiness must all pass.

capabilities.name: Narrator
capabilities.purpose: Make the game funny, keep the player moving, and turn play into the story of this Karl.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player laughs, receives useful guidance, and recognises a coherent character arc across the life.
capabilities.currentTruth: The narrator prioritises authored story, behavior, memory, baked pair lines, optional live copy, grammar, and generic fallback.
capabilities.approvedTarget: Humour, guidance, and story continuity remain equally required across generated gameplay, seeded lives, longer memory, and online production.
qualitativeAcceptance: Players laugh at or quote a reaction.
Players act on narrator guidance when stuck.
Players can describe who their Karl became.

lifecycle.advancementGate: Playtest must independently evidence humour, guidance, and story continuity.

capabilities.name: Pursue needs
capabilities.purpose: Give clear short-term goals without reducing the game to one prescribed recipe.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player can name the next need and imagine multiple possible solutions.
capabilities.currentTruth: Current Act problems, predicates, hints, and alternative canonical solutions guide progression.
capabilities.approvedTarget: Canonical discoveries and validated inventions can provide multiple legible paths to the same need.
qualitativeAcceptance: Players can name the current goal.
Players perceive multiple possible solution paths.
Players do not feel railroaded.

lifecycle.advancementGate: Generated solutions must pass the same deterministic solve predicates as canonical elements.

capabilities.name: Face challenges and sidequests
capabilities.purpose: Create temporary priority conflicts that make lives diverge.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player notices an interruption, chooses deliberately, and later recognises its consequence.
capabilities.currentTruth: Timed challenges can spawn, tick, resolve, fail, and affect endings. Sidequest variation is not yet governed by the life seed.
capabilities.approvedTarget: Seeded sidequests and challenges interrupt plans without replacing the main story, and their consequences remain visible later.
qualitativeAcceptance: Players notice the priority conflict.
Players deliberately change or preserve their plan.
Players connect a later outcome to the choice.

lifecycle.advancementGate: Seeded challenge selection must preserve life viability and causal evidence.

capabilities.name: Read one life's Chronicle
capabilities.purpose: Preserve the causal story of one distinct Karl life.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player can reconstruct what this Karl tried, discovered, invented, solved, and became.
capabilities.currentTruth: The Living Chronicle shows the narrator, latest outcome, canonical archive, timeline, and—when enabled—a separate invention section.
capabilities.approvedTarget: Every archived life can be reconstructed from attempts, discoveries, inventions, needs, challenges, branches, and fate.
qualitativeAcceptance: Players reconstruct the causal story of one life.
Players distinguish one archived Karl from another.
Canonical history and inventions remain visibly distinct.

lifecycle.advancementGate: Versioned per-life archives and save migration must be specified and tested.

capabilities.name: Complete the master compendium
capabilities.purpose: Make finite authored completion legible and motivate another life without revealing exact recipes.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player understands completion, identifies a broad gap, and chooses another life to pursue it.
capabilities.currentTruth: Discoveries and fates persist locally, but there is no unified authored-content percentage or archived-life model.
capabilities.approvedTarget: The compendium combines canonical discoveries, major branches, and endings into a percentage while inventions remain in a separate unbounded gallery.
qualitativeAcceptance: Players understand what the completion percentage includes.
Players identify an unexplored area without receiving an exact solution.
Players choose another life to pursue the gap.

lifecycle.advancementGate: Define branch identity, completion denominator, persistence, and migration before implementation.

capabilities.name: Unlock a fate
capabilities.purpose: Reward exploration with a surprising, collectible ending.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player unlocks a memorable fate, understands its cause, and becomes curious about undiscovered endings.
capabilities.currentTruth: Authored endings unlock from deterministic state and appear as persistent fates.
capabilities.approvedTarget: Each ending remains surprising but causally traceable, and its rarity/conditions never require fabricated statistics.
qualitativeAcceptance: The ending surprises the player.
The player can trace why this life produced it.
The player wants to collect more fates.

lifecycle.advancementGate: Persistent compendium semantics and ending provenance must be defined.

capabilities.name: Replay and optionally share
capabilities.purpose: Turn completion gaps, new seeds, sidequests, and alternative progression into another distinct life. Sharing expresses the result but is not required for progression.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player names a new target and voluntarily begins another life; sharing remains optional expression.
capabilities.currentTruth: Players can start a new life and copy a run summary. Life archives and shareable seeds are not yet implemented.
capabilities.approvedTarget: Endings and compendium gaps present meaningful replay targets; life summaries and seeds remain understandable outside the running game.
qualitativeAcceptance: Players name a different target or path.
Players voluntarily begin another life.
Shared summaries remain understandable without being required for progress.

lifecycle.advancementGate: Seed format, life archive, and compendium targets must be implemented and playtested.

capabilities.name: Play across devices
capabilities.purpose: Deliver the same meaningful, completable game on phone and desktop, even when layout and input differ.
capabilities.playerOutcome: The player understands the same story, choices, feedback, and collection on supported devices.
capabilities.currentTruth: One Vite web application serves responsive mobile and desktop layouts. Local saves are browser-local.
capabilities.approvedTarget: The Svelte replacement preserves meaning, behavior, accessibility, events, and save compatibility across supported devices.
qualitativeAcceptance: The same life is completable on phone and desktop.
Layout differences do not change product meaning.
Every capability passes equivalent-channel accessibility and WCAG AA.

lifecycle.advancementGate: Differential old/new parity must pass before Svelte replaces the current UI.
